pathway.title: Millicom International Cellular S.A. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: 1. The credit story is a consolidation story. Nine-month 2026 revenue of 6,440 and Adjusted EBITDA of 2,958 compare with 4,150 and 1,964 a year earlier, but the release attributes most of the growth to perimeter and currency, with organic revenue growth of 4.4 percent and organic Adjusted EBITDA growth of 8.8 percent. Basis: CP-1 figures and the CP-1A volume-drivers and Colombia transaction rows. Category: Documentary Fact for the figures; the reading that organic growth is the better durability guide is Analyst Interpretation. Mechanism: acquired revenue lifts coverage but has a short record under Millicom control. Implication: durability should be judged on organic trends and on the Colombian integration outcome. 2. Leverage has improved for two consecutive quarters but is measured on a management basis that cannot be reproduced. Management leverage fell from 2.76x at March 31, 2026 to 2.73x and then 2.53x at September 30, 2026, against a year-end target of below 2.5x. Simple net debt over reported last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA is 2.14x and 2.99x when lease liabilities are added (CP-1 Calculation 3). Category: Documentary Fact for the reported ratio and Analyst Interpretation for the simple ratios. Mechanism: lease costs are subtracted in the management denominator and acquisitions are pro forma, neither bridge is supplied. Implication: use the lease-inclusive view alongside the headline ratio, and treat the 2.5x target as a management claim. 3. Debt service capacity is supported by cash generation but nearly all of it is claimed by fixed uses. Nine-month Adjusted EBITDA of 2,958 covers interest on bonds and bank financing of 472 about 6.3 times and covers that plus lease interest about 4.2 times (CP-1 Calculation 6); equity free cash flow of 867 was followed by dividends paid of 587, leaving about 280 against acquisition payments of 924. Category: Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation. Mechanism: lease payments, spectrum and taxes are the largest fixed claims ahead of equity free cash flow. Implication: cushion for unplanned shocks is thinner than the headline EBITDA suggests. 4. Liquidity relies on refinancing access. Cash of 848 equals debt due within one year of 872; the 2027 SEK note and the 600 revolving facility, which was undrawn at December 31, 2025 and due October 2027, mature within about fourteen months, and the facility's current availability is Not supplied. Category: Documentary Fact for balances and maturities, Insufficient Information for facility availability. Mechanism: local bank facilities have been rolled routinely in 2026 and bond market access was shown by the 2032 notes reopening, but a dislocation would hit the near-term ladder first. Implication: monitor facility status and the 2027 maturities. 5. Shareholder distributions are rising at the same time as leverage is being reduced. The Board approved an interim dividend of $1.50 per share in August 2026 on top of the regular $3.00 per share cycle; the controlling shareholder group holds about 42.2 percent of voting shares. Scheduled cash dividends of about 629 follow September 30, 2026 (CP-1 Calculation 7). Category: Documentary Fact for the declared amounts; Analyst Interpretation for the pressure on deleveraging. Mechanism: distributions compete with debt reduction for equity free cash flow. Implication: neutral to mixed behaviour on the evidence, because capacity limits in the debt documents are not supplied. 6. Control and related-party links are concentrated. One shareholder group holds de facto control and four of eight non-executive board seats; a payable to the Iliad Holding Group of 195 at December 31, 2025 has no stated nature, and the Chile investment is held with NJJ, a party linked to the controlling shareholder. Category: Documentary Fact; absence of documented creditor-adverse actions is not evidence of contractual protection. Implication: governance risk is moderated by alignment but cannot be sized without the indentures. 7. Data quality and definition risk limit precision. The December 31, 2025 balance sheet was restated, 2025 comparatives were re-presented, Coltel and Ecuador purchase accounting is provisional, Q1 and Q3 statements are unreviewed, the Chile earn-out is stated as up to $150 million in the 20-F and up to $490 million in the 6-Ks (conflict C1), and 9M operating cash flow differs by 9 between the cash flow statement and the release reconciliation. Category: Documentary Fact. Implication: carry both values and label bases; do not treat any single reconciled figure as settled.

cells.text: Provider of fixed and mobile services in emerging markets of Latin America under the Tigo and Tigo Business brands, serving "eleven countries in Latin America"
20-F chunk 77: "We are a leading provider of fixed and mobile services dedicated to emerging markets." ("leading" is the issuer's characterisation)
Diversified by country but all exposure is emerging-market Latin America, so currency, regulatory and macro shocks are correlated at region level

Two service categories: Mobile (data, voice, SMS, mobile financial services) and Fixed and other (broadband, pay-TV, fixed voice, B2B); plus equipment sales. Mobile was 60 percent of 2025 service revenue and fixed and other 38 percent
20-F chunks 79-80; nine months 2026 service revenue split in Q3 6-K chunk 19 (Mobile 3,668; Cable and other fixed 2,283; Other 94; total service revenue 6,045)
Recurring service revenue is the base of cash flow; prepaid mobile is paid in advance, which supports working capital, while equipment revenue is lower margin
Prepaid-to-postpaid migration and a "more-for-more" pricing strategy
Q3 6-K chunk 29: "We are also executing a clear more-for-more pricing strategy."

Pricing power is asserted, not evidenced independently; the release gives mobile ARPU and postpaid growth (CP-1) as supporting data. Inflation and purchasing power in Bolivia and the Middle East energy effect are named risks (Q3 6-K chunk 33)
Mobile customers 55,845 thousand and postpaid 17,194 thousand at September 30, 2026; homes passed 22,792 thousand; customer relationships 5,966 thousand
Q3 6-K chunk 33 (KPIs exclude the Honduras joint venture). Growth is "primarily driven by the inclusion of Coltel and our operations in Ecuador and Uruguay"
Most customer growth is acquired, not organic; the release states excluding M&A the postpaid base grew 0.9 million and HFC/FTTH revenue-generating units "would have declined by 434,000"

Operating segments follow countries: Guatemala, Tigo Colombia, Coltel, Panama, Paraguay, Ecuador, Honduras (joint venture, shown at 100 percent), Chile (associate, shown at 100 percent), and Other (El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica, Uruguay, Bolivia)
The two equity-accounted segments are eliminated from group totals, so group cash flow includes them only through dividends and repatriation (79 for nine months, CP-1)
Nine-month 2026 segment revenue before eliminations: Guatemala 1,314; Tigo Colombia 1,354; Coltel 1,127; total segments 7,936; group 6,440
Q3 6-K chunk 17. In 2025 Guatemala was 26 percent and Colombia 22 percent of segment revenue (20-F chunk 101)

Colombia is now two consolidated segments of the largest country exposure; a Colombian shock or peso move has more weight than a year earlier. The credit quality of the Guatemala operating entity matters because it carries the 5.125% notes due 2032

Main cost lines are equipment, programming and other direct costs and operating expenses, then depreciation and amortization; Q3 2026 restructuring and one-off items above Adjusted EBITDA were 31 and 149 for nine months, mainly in Colombia
Integration costs are being expensed through Adjusted EBITDA; management says restructuring is included in its 2026 targets (Q2 6-K chunk 32). Whether further severance is planned is Not disclosed
Capex excluding spectrum of 669 for nine months 2026; spectrum paid 207; payables and accruals for capital expenditure of 2,101 at September 30, 2026
Spectrum and capex obligations are a recurring cash claim; large capex payables are a debt-like supplier-funding channel outside gross debt
Group sold its Central American towers (Lati) to SBA and leased back sites for 15 years; lease liabilities were 3,190 at September 30, 2026
The disposal converted owned assets into long-term lease obligations; lease payments (net 483 for nine months, CP-1) rank ahead of equity cash flow
Change in working capital contributed 19 for nine months 2026 against (74) for nine months 2025
Supports cash conversion in the period; mixed with a 903 rise in capex payables since December 31, 2025 (CP-1 gap G9)
The interim notes state operations "are not affected by significant seasonal or cyclical patterns"; the CEO called Q1 "typically our weakest quarter" for equity free cash flow
Quarterly cash flow is uneven; spot net debt at a quarter-end may not represent the annual average
61 percent of gross debt is in local currency or swapped; 56 percent is fixed rate; the dollar-denominated debt carries 5.7 percent average interest and the group 8.3 percent

Local-currency debt hedges revenue currencies but adds higher coupons; appreciation of the Colombian peso, Paraguayan guarani and Boliviano raised reported results and local-currency debt in dollars (Q3 6-K chunk 33)
Spectrum licenses carry expiries; the earliest are 2026 in Guatemala and Paraguay, and Colombia permits for 15 MHz in 1900 MHz and 20 MHz AWS "have expired" with renewal filed
License renewal costs and the timing of 2026 expiries are a liquidity and operating risk; renewal fees are not quantified (Insufficient Information)
The 20-F says there is no significant concentration of credit risk "except for certain B2B customers (mainly governments)"
Government receivables could delay collections; the size of government customers is Not disclosed
Tigo Money operates in five markets; the group's priority is a partial or full divestiture, and the Paraguay MFS business is classified as held for sale (discontinued operations)
Small contribution; sale proceeds base price 10 with a potential 7 earn-out (Q3 6-K chunk 12)
Churn, postpaid versus prepaid margin, pro forma Coltel Adjusted EBITDA, fixed-line EBITDA by country for Q3 and customer concentration by size
Not located in the four sources
These would test margin resilience and acquired-asset performance; Missing evidence is not an adverse conclusion

runs.text: Strengths. - Scale and diversification. Category: Documentary Fact. Revenue streams are recurring and spread across twelve countries, with Mobile and Fixed services, and the largest segments are Guatemala and the two Colombian segments. Mechanism: geographic spread reduces the effect of any single market. Basis: CP-1A company and concentration rows and CP-1 revenue figures. - Strong and growing cash generation. Category: Documentary Fact. Nine-month Adjusted EBITDA of 2,958, operating cash flow of 2,289 and equity free cash flow of 867, with management guidance of around 1.1 billion for 2026 (Management Language, qualified). Mechanism: cash generation funds interest, leases and capex and supports deleveraging. - Improving leverage trajectory. Category: Documentary Fact. Management leverage 2.53x at September 30, 2026 compared with 2.73x and 2.76x in the prior two quarters; net debt was stable quarter over quarter at 7,983. Mechanism: higher EBITDA and EFCF are offsetting acquisition debt. - Funding diversification. Category: Documentary Fact. Bonds, bank loans, development finance institution loans and local-currency issuance at both corporate and operating levels; about 70 percent of debt is at operating entities and 30 percent at the corporate level. Mechanism: reduces dependence on a single market; but structural subordination of corporate creditors to operating-level debt is also implied (Analyst Interpretation). - Local-currency matching and hedging. Category: Documentary Fact. 61 percent of gross debt is in local currency or swapped, and the 2027 SEK note is swapped to dollars. Mechanism: aligns debt with revenue currencies. - Transparent, frequent reporting and a no-breach statement. Category: Documentary Fact. Quarterly releases with reconciliations; the 20-F states no covenant breach at December 31, 2025 and none anticipated for twelve months. Limitation: that statement is not updated in the 2026 reports and thresholds are Not supplied (Insufficient Information).

Weaknesses. - High absolute leverage and lease burden. Category: Documentary Fact. Net debt of 7,983 and lease liabilities of 3,190; lease-inclusive net financing obligations of 11,173 against reported last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of 3,734 (Analyst Interpretation on the ratio). Mechanism: leases rank as fixed charges and the tower leaseback increased them. - Emerging-market, correlated exposure and currency volatility. Category: Documentary Fact. The release cites rapid appreciation of the Colombian peso, Paraguayan guarani and Boliviano and a regime change in Bolivia. Mechanism: reported dollar results and local-currency debt values swing with exchange rates; reversal would reduce dollar EBITDA. - Integration and execution risk in Colombia. Category: Documentary Fact for the restructuring charges and the Coltel net loss; Analyst Interpretation for the risk. Mechanism: severance and integration costs reduce EBITDA and cash flow and delay synergies. - Floating-rate exposure and cost of debt. Category: Documentary Fact. Fixed-rate debt fell to 56 percent of debt and the average interest rate was 8.3 percent. Mechanism: higher rates pass through to interest expense; rate sensitivity is Not supplied (Insufficient Information). - Near-term maturities and facility dependence. Category: Documentary Fact. Cash of 848 against debt due within one year of 872. Mechanism: refinancing needs are recurring. - Controlling shareholder influence and distributions. Category: Documentary Fact. See key finding 5 and 6. - Provisional accounting and limited legal visibility. Category: Insufficient Information. Covenant definitions, indentures, guarantor groups and the revolving facility position are not in the evidence set, so legal capacity for distributions, asset transfers and priming cannot be assessed.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The set contains no single leveraged-finance transaction; the creditor-relevant transactions are the 2025 and 2026 acquisitions, the asset monetization and the 2026 financings. Each item is a Documentary Fact from the filings unless it says otherwise.

Colombia consolidation. On January 27, 2026 Millicom was awarded 100 percent of EPM's remaining shares in UNE EPM Telecomunicaciones S.A. at a price of COP 418,741 per share, about COP 2.1 trillion (about $571 million); the deal closed January 29, 2026 and was accounted for as an equity transaction that reduced equity by $627 million (Q3 6-K chunk 8). On February 6, 2026 it closed the purchase of Telefónica's controlling 67.5 percent of Colombia Telecomunicaciones S.A. E.S.P. (Coltel) for about $214.4 million, of which $169 million was paid at acquisition (Q3 6-K chunk 9). Coltel was acquired with "Other debt and financing" of $1,424 million and lease liabilities of $515 million at fair value, and contributed revenue of $1,127 million and a net loss of $168 million from acquisition to September 30, 2026, including about $71 million of severance (Q3 6-K chunks 9-10). On April 27, 2026 it bought the remaining 32.5 percent from La Nación, a $219 million equity transaction (Q3 6-K chunk 9). The purchase accounting remains provisional. Creditor mechanic: control of the combined Colombian business is now full, which removes minority leakage and approvals but added acquired debt and integration costs; the management leverage rose to 2.76x at March 31, 2026 before falling to 2.53x at September 30, 2026 (CP-1). The Colombian joint operations (UNIRED and UT) are consolidated in full from the Coltel acquisition, and EPM remains a non-controlling partner in certain operations (Q3 6-K chunks 5, 22).

Ecuador and Uruguay. Millicom completed the purchase of Telefónica Móviles del Uruguay on October 7, 2025 for an enterprise value of $440 million and of Telefónica's Ecuador operations on October 30, 2025 for an enterprise value of $380 million (Q3 6-K chunks 13-14). Uruguay accounting is final; Ecuador's measurement period ended October 30, 2026 and was still being finalized when the statements were issued. Both carry local bank debt; a payment guaranty from MIC S.A. supports the Uruguay Santander loan (20-F chunk 256).

Chile with NJJ. On February 10, 2026 Celtel Chile, S.L. (49 percent Millicom, 51 percent NJJ Cactus SAS) bought Telefónica Móviles Chile for $50 million cash with contingent earn-outs "without recourse to Millicom"; Celtel carries a recognized liability of $110 million at September 30, 2026, funded by external financial debt, and mutual call options exist from the fifth and sixth anniversaries (Q3 6-K chunk 11). It is equity-accounted and the carrying value is nil because losses exceeded the investment, leaving $41 million of unrecognized losses at Millicom's share (Q3 6-K chunk 22). The 20-F describes the earn-out as up to $150 million (20-F chunk 297) and the 6-Ks as up to $490 million (see Conflicts). NJJ is described in the related party note as part of Xavier Niel's holdings (20-F chunk 295), so this is a joint investment with a party linked to the controlling shareholder; terms are as disclosed and the pricing basis of the options is not quantified.

Tower monetization and leaseback. On October 28, 2024 Millicom agreed to sell Lati International and other assets, more than 7,000 towers in Central America, to SBA Communications Corp. with a 15-year leaseback and a build-to-suit commitment for up to 2,500 further sites; Lati Paraguay was sold to Atis Group on June 3, 2025; the gain recognized in 2025 was $741 million (Q3 6-K chunks 14-15). Millicom retains Lati subsidiaries in Bolivia with about 2,000 towers (20-F chunk 91). Creditor mechanic (Analyst Interpretation): the sale converted owned assets into leased ones, so the leaseback added lease liabilities that rank as fixed claims; how the proceeds were applied is not stated in the sources reviewed.

Other portfolio actions. Tigo Paraguay signed on January 5, 2026 to sell its mobile finance business for a base price of $10 million with a potential $7 million earn-out (Q3 6-K chunk 12). The planned merger of Tigo Costa Rica with Liberty Latin America (agreement of August 1, 2024) was rejected by the regulator SUTEL in September and November 2025 (20-F chunk 83); the Costa Rica unit recorded a goodwill impairment of about $32 million in 2026, with goodwill of about $123 million remaining (Q3 6-K chunks 27-28). Tigo Sports local content was sold to FOX (agreement announced April 13, 2026; Q1 6-K chunk 22).

New debt issues and refinancings in 2026 (all subsequent to the 20-F balance sheet date). MIC S.A. reopened its 7.375% Senior Notes due 2032 for an additional $87.5 million in a Regulation S private placement on April 14, 2026, admitted to the Euro MTF market, placed with Banco General, S.A.; MIC S.A. issued an 8-year COP-USD linked private bond for COP 370,000 million at a fixed rate on March 27, 2026, subscribed by the Inter-American Development Bank and Proparco (Q3 6-K chunk 24). Tigo Paraguay redeemed its 5.875% notes due 2027, about $139.7 million, at par on April 29, 2026 (Q3 6-K chunk 25). Coltel entered a one-year $100 million bridge facility with Banco Santander at variable rate on April 13, 2026 to repay a $100 million HSBC facility, and later new three-year and one-year variable bank loans in Colombian pesos; Tigo Colombia added a four-year variable loan with Davivienda of COP 220,000 million; Tigo Panama refinanced a $75 million loan with a new six-year BAC loan in August 2026; Tigo Guatemala, Tigo Bolivia and others added bank loans (Q3 6-K chunks 23-25). After the quarter, Coltel took a COP 40,000 million BTG Pactual loan and prepaid $12.5 million of the Santander loan on October 15, 2026 (Q3 6-K chunk 28, subsequent event). Instrument-level terms such as ranking, security, covenants and guarantor groups are Not supplied for these issues, and use of proceeds is stated only for the Coltel bridge. Gross debt rose from $6,886 million to $8,648 million over the nine months (CP-1).

Capital returns. The AGM of May 20, 2026 approved a dividend of $3.00 per share in four quarterly installments and the Board on August 5, 2026 approved an interim dividend of $1.50 per share payable in January and April 2027 (Q3 6-K chunk 20). Share repurchases were $119 million in 2025 and none in the nine months of 2026 (20-F chunk 198; Q3 6-K chunk 5).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Colombia consolidation. On January 27, 2026 Millicom was awarded 100 percent of EPM's remaining shares in UNE EPM Telecomunicaciones S.A. at a price of COP 418,741 per share, about COP 2.1 trillion (about $571 million); the deal closed January 29, 2026 and was accounted for as an equity transaction that reduced equity by $627 million (Q3 6-K chunk 8). On February 6, 2026 it closed the purchase of Telefónica's controlling 67.5 percent of Colombia Telecomunicaciones S.A. E.S.P. (Coltel) for about $214.4 million, of which $169 million was paid at acquisition (Q3 6-K chunk 9). Coltel was acquired with "Other debt and financing" of $1,424 million and lease liabilities of $515 million at fair value, and contributed revenue of $1,127 million and a net loss of $168 million from acquisition to September 30, 2026, including about $71 million of severance (Q3 6-K chunks 9-10). On April 27, 2026 it bought the remaining 32.5 percent from La Nación, a $219 million equity transaction (Q3 6-K chunk 9). The purchase accounting remains provisional. Creditor mechanic: control of the combined Colombian business is now full, which removes minority leakage and approvals but added acquired debt and integration costs; the management leverage rose to 2.76x at March 31, 2026 before falling to 2.53x at September 30, 2026 (CP-1). The Colombian joint operations (UNIRED and UT) are consolidated in full from the Coltel acquisition, and EPM remains a non-controlling partner in certain operations (Q3 6-K chunks 5, 22).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ecuador and Uruguay. Millicom completed the purchase of Telefónica Móviles del Uruguay on October 7, 2025 for an enterprise value of $440 million and of Telefónica's Ecuador operations on October 30, 2025 for an enterprise value of $380 million (Q3 6-K chunks 13-14). Uruguay accounting is final; Ecuador's measurement period ended October 30, 2026 and was still being finalized when the statements were issued. Both carry local bank debt; a payment guaranty from MIC S.A. supports the Uruguay Santander loan (20-F chunk 256).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Chile with NJJ. On February 10, 2026 Celtel Chile, S.L. (49 percent Millicom, 51 percent NJJ Cactus SAS) bought Telefónica Móviles Chile for $50 million cash with contingent earn-outs "without recourse to Millicom"; Celtel carries a recognized liability of $110 million at September 30, 2026, funded by external financial debt, and mutual call options exist from the fifth and sixth anniversaries (Q3 6-K chunk 11). It is equity-accounted and the carrying value is nil because losses exceeded the investment, leaving $41 million of unrecognized losses at Millicom's share (Q3 6-K chunk 22). The 20-F describes the earn-out as up to $150 million (20-F chunk 297) and the 6-Ks as up to $490 million (see Conflicts). NJJ is described in the related party note as part of Xavier Niel's holdings (20-F chunk 295), so this is a joint investment with a party linked to the controlling shareholder; terms are as disclosed and the pricing basis of the options is not quantified.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Tower monetization and leaseback. On October 28, 2024 Millicom agreed to sell Lati International and other assets, more than 7,000 towers in Central America, to SBA Communications Corp. with a 15-year leaseback and a build-to-suit commitment for up to 2,500 further sites; Lati Paraguay was sold to Atis Group on June 3, 2025; the gain recognized in 2025 was $741 million (Q3 6-K chunks 14-15). Millicom retains Lati subsidiaries in Bolivia with about 2,000 towers (20-F chunk 91). Creditor mechanic (Analyst Interpretation): the sale converted owned assets into leased ones, so the leaseback added lease liabilities that rank as fixed claims; how the proceeds were applied is not stated in the sources reviewed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Other portfolio actions. Tigo Paraguay signed on January 5, 2026 to sell its mobile finance business for a base price of $10 million with a potential $7 million earn-out (Q3 6-K chunk 12). The planned merger of Tigo Costa Rica with Liberty Latin America (agreement of August 1, 2024) was rejected by the regulator SUTEL in September and November 2025 (20-F chunk 83); the Costa Rica unit recorded a goodwill impairment of about $32 million in 2026, with goodwill of about $123 million remaining (Q3 6-K chunks 27-28). Tigo Sports local content was sold to FOX (agreement announced April 13, 2026; Q1 6-K chunk 22).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt issues and refinancings in 2026 (all subsequent to the 20-F balance sheet date). MIC S.A. reopened its 7.375% Senior Notes due 2032 for an additional $87.5 million in a Regulation S private placement on April 14, 2026, admitted to the Euro MTF market, placed with Banco General, S.A.; MIC S.A. issued an 8-year COP-USD linked private bond for COP 370,000 million at a fixed rate on March 27, 2026, subscribed by the Inter-American Development Bank and Proparco (Q3 6-K chunk 24). Tigo Paraguay redeemed its 5.875% notes due 2027, about $139.7 million, at par on April 29, 2026 (Q3 6-K chunk 25). Coltel entered a one-year $100 million bridge facility with Banco Santander at variable rate on April 13, 2026 to repay a $100 million HSBC facility, and later new three-year and one-year variable bank loans in Colombian pesos; Tigo Colombia added a four-year variable loan with Davivienda of COP 220,000 million; Tigo Panama refinanced a $75 million loan with a new six-year BAC loan in August 2026; Tigo Guatemala, Tigo Bolivia and others added bank loans (Q3 6-K chunks 23-25). After the quarter, Coltel took a COP 40,000 million BTG Pactual loan and prepaid $12.5 million of the Santander loan on October 15, 2026 (Q3 6-K chunk 28, subsequent event). Instrument-level terms such as ranking, security, covenants and guarantor groups are Not supplied for these issues, and use of proceeds is stated only for the Coltel bridge. Gross debt rose from $6,886 million to $8,648 million over the nine months (CP-1).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital returns. The AGM of May 20, 2026 approved a dividend of $3.00 per share in four quarterly installments and the Board on August 5, 2026 approved an interim dividend of $1.50 per share payable in January and April 2027 (Q3 6-K chunk 20). Share repurchases were $119 million in 2025 and none in the nine months of 2026 (20-F chunk 198; Q3 6-K chunk 5).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: service revenue of 6,045 for nine months 2026 against 3,888, with organic service revenue growth of 5.3 percent (Q3 6-K chunk 41), most of the growth coming from consolidating Coltel, Ecuador and Uruguay. Mechanism: recurring subscription revenue across twelve countries gives scale, and prepaid-to-postpaid migration raises visibility, but the acquired revenue base has a short history under Millicom control and the underlying organic rate is mid-single-digit. Implication: revenue is large and recurring; the comparison to prior years is flattered by perimeter, so organic growth is the better guide to durability. Conflict that counters it: none logged.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: Adjusted EBITDA margin of 45.9 percent for nine months 2026 against 47.3 percent, with 149 of one-off items above Adjusted EBITDA (Q3 6-K chunks 34, 41). Mechanism: Coltel integration and restructuring are depressing near-term margin and consuming cash, while lease payments and spectrum are fixed claims. Implication: coverage and free cash flow depend on delivering the Colombian cost program; if integration slips, equity free cash flow guidance is at risk (management claim). Conflict that counters it: C3 does not change cash flow; the unreconciled operating cash flow figures in CP-1 gap G5 limit precision.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Concentration risk. Evidence: Guatemala and the two Colombian segments carry the largest segment revenue and the Guatemala entity issues $900 million 5.125% notes with subsidiary guarantees. Mechanism: a regulatory, currency or macro event in one of these countries affects a large share of consolidated EBITDA and the operating-level debt serviced from it. Implication: monitor country-level cash availability and the share of debt at operating entities (about 70 percent, Q3 6-K chunk 32), noting that MIC S.A. is dependent on upstream dividends (20-F chunk 111).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Sponsor alignment. Evidence: controlling shareholder holds about 42.2 percent, appoints four of eight non-executive directors, and has a related-party payable and a joint investment. Mechanism: aligned equity ownership can support the issuer, but larger distributions (a $1.50 interim on top of the regular dividend) and a related investment competing for cash with creditors are potential leakage channels. Implication: neutral to mixed on documented actions; the absence of documented creditor-adverse actions is not evidence that covenants prevent them because indentures are not supplied. Conflict that counters it: C2.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. Key uncertainties. Evidence: Coltel and Ecuador purchase accounting provisional; covenant terms, debt schedule and revolving facility status not supplied; Chile earn-out size in conflict (C1); Guatemala litigation settled but other claims remain. Mechanism: each limits the ability to size liquidity and covenant headroom. Implication: committee readiness is limited until the named documents are obtained.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rationale (evidence, mechanism, implication): Millicom is a large, scaled, recurring-revenue operator across twelve Latin American countries whose earnings base has stepped up sharply through the 2025 and 2026 acquisitions in Colombia, Ecuador and Uruguay. The consolidated net debt increased from 5,357 at December 31, 2025 to 7,983 at September 30, 2026, and management leverage moved from 2.17x to a peak of 2.76x and then to 2.53x at September 30, 2026. The mechanism is that purchase payments, consolidated acquired debt and a heavier lease and dividend burden were absorbed by a much larger EBITDA and equity free cash flow base; deleveraging now depends on integrating Colombia and delivering the stated cash flow. The credit implication is a business with sound operating scale and improving cash generation but with high absolute leverage, material lease obligations outside the headline measure, a near-term maturity and refinancing agenda and an incomplete view of covenant headroom. The fundamental view is therefore that debt service capacity appears supported on the reported period, with the quality of that support limited by perimeter effects, definition risk and missing legal documents. The confidence is Medium rather than High because covenant terms, instrument-level debt after December 31, 2025, the revolving facility position and indentures are not in the evidence set.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Thesis (Category: Analyst Interpretation): a scaled Latin American telecom group with recurring cash flows and improving but still elevated leverage after a step-change in Colombian consolidation: debt service looks supported by reported earnings and equity free cash flow, while integration delivery, shareholder distributions, refinancing and unsupplied covenant terms determine how much headroom actually exists.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. The credit story is a consolidation story. Nine-month 2026 revenue of 6,440 and Adjusted EBITDA of 2,958 compare with 4,150 and 1,964 a year earlier, but the release attributes most of the growth to perimeter and currency, with organic revenue growth of 4.4 percent and organic Adjusted EBITDA growth of 8.8 percent. Basis: CP-1 figures and the CP-1A volume-drivers and Colombia transaction rows. Category: Documentary Fact for the figures; the reading that organic growth is the better durability guide is Analyst Interpretation. Mechanism: acquired revenue lifts coverage but has a short record under Millicom control. Implication: durability should be judged on organic trends and on the Colombian integration outcome.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Leverage has improved for two consecutive quarters but is measured on a management basis that cannot be reproduced. Management leverage fell from 2.76x at March 31, 2026 to 2.73x and then 2.53x at September 30, 2026, against a year-end target of below 2.5x. Simple net debt over reported last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA is 2.14x and 2.99x when lease liabilities are added (CP-1 Calculation 3). Category: Documentary Fact for the reported ratio and Analyst Interpretation for the simple ratios. Mechanism: lease costs are subtracted in the management denominator and acquisitions are pro forma, neither bridge is supplied. Implication: use the lease-inclusive view alongside the headline ratio, and treat the 2.5x target as a management claim.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Debt service capacity is supported by cash generation but nearly all of it is claimed by fixed uses. Nine-month Adjusted EBITDA of 2,958 covers interest on bonds and bank financing of 472 about 6.3 times and covers that plus lease interest about 4.2 times (CP-1 Calculation 6); equity free cash flow of 867 was followed by dividends paid of 587, leaving about 280 against acquisition payments of 924. Category: Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation. Mechanism: lease payments, spectrum and taxes are the largest fixed claims ahead of equity free cash flow. Implication: cushion for unplanned shocks is thinner than the headline EBITDA suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Liquidity relies on refinancing access. Cash of 848 equals debt due within one year of 872; the 2027 SEK note and the 600 revolving facility, which was undrawn at December 31, 2025 and due October 2027, mature within about fourteen months, and the facility's current availability is Not supplied. Category: Documentary Fact for balances and maturities, Insufficient Information for facility availability. Mechanism: local bank facilities have been rolled routinely in 2026 and bond market access was shown by the 2032 notes reopening, but a dislocation would hit the near-term ladder first. Implication: monitor facility status and the 2027 maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. Shareholder distributions are rising at the same time as leverage is being reduced. The Board approved an interim dividend of $1.50 per share in August 2026 on top of the regular $3.00 per share cycle; the controlling shareholder group holds about 42.2 percent of voting shares. Scheduled cash dividends of about 629 follow September 30, 2026 (CP-1 Calculation 7). Category: Documentary Fact for the declared amounts; Analyst Interpretation for the pressure on deleveraging. Mechanism: distributions compete with debt reduction for equity free cash flow. Implication: neutral to mixed behaviour on the evidence, because capacity limits in the debt documents are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 6. Control and related-party links are concentrated. One shareholder group holds de facto control and four of eight non-executive board seats; a payable to the Iliad Holding Group of 195 at December 31, 2025 has no stated nature, and the Chile investment is held with NJJ, a party linked to the controlling shareholder. Category: Documentary Fact; absence of documented creditor-adverse actions is not evidence of contractual protection. Implication: governance risk is moderated by alignment but cannot be sized without the indentures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 7. Data quality and definition risk limit precision. The December 31, 2025 balance sheet was restated, 2025 comparatives were re-presented, Coltel and Ecuador purchase accounting is provisional, Q1 and Q3 statements are unreviewed, the Chile earn-out is stated as up to $150 million in the 20-F and up to $490 million in the 6-Ks (conflict C1), and 9M operating cash flow differs by 9 between the cash flow statement and the release reconciliation. Category: Documentary Fact. Implication: carry both values and label bases; do not treat any single reconciled figure as settled.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Scale and diversification. Category: Documentary Fact. Revenue streams are recurring and spread across twelve countries, with Mobile and Fixed services, and the largest segments are Guatemala and the two Colombian segments. Mechanism: geographic spread reduces the effect of any single market. Basis: CP-1A company and concentration rows and CP-1 revenue figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Strong and growing cash generation. Category: Documentary Fact. Nine-month Adjusted EBITDA of 2,958, operating cash flow of 2,289 and equity free cash flow of 867, with management guidance of around 1.1 billion for 2026 (Management Language, qualified). Mechanism: cash generation funds interest, leases and capex and supports deleveraging.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Improving leverage trajectory. Category: Documentary Fact. Management leverage 2.53x at September 30, 2026 compared with 2.73x and 2.76x in the prior two quarters; net debt was stable quarter over quarter at 7,983. Mechanism: higher EBITDA and EFCF are offsetting acquisition debt.

Bonds, bank loans, development finance institution loans and local-currency issuance at both corporate and operating levels; about 70 percent of debt is at operating entities and 30 percent at the corporate level. Mechanism: reduces dependence on a single market; but structural subordination of corporate creditors to operating-level debt is also implied (Analyst Interpretation).
